key_insight: Human-rewarded experience can teach agents task–conduct tradeoffs and increase resistance to later task-only training, though it does not guarantee violation-free behavior.
engineering_relevance: Alignment design should account for training environments, retained experience, and deployment safeguards—not just assigned objectives.
method: Model evolutionary selection where only agents taking the rewarded action reproduce.
Compare task-only, fixed linear, and learned policies under conflicting task and conduct rewards.
Examine accumulated experience, finite memory, and hard prohibitions.
evidence_signal: Theoretical results and small-neural-network experiments illustrate how reward targets and memory affect learned tradeoffs and resistance to subsequent training.
watch_item: Violations can occur before an agent’s prevailing disposition changes; hard prohibitions may prevent them but can be costly if mispecified.
paper_title: Alignment by Socialization: Learning Tradeoffs Under Selection
